Here's a highly advanced Keras project for a seasoned AI/ML engineer—building on cutting-edge research for unsupervised anomaly detection in multivariate time series using an Attention‑based ConvLSTM Autoencoder with Dynamic Thresholding.

Project Title

attention_convlstm_anomaly_detection.py

▶️ Short Description

Implement an unsupervised Attention‑ConvLSTM autoencoder leveraging feature-image construction from multivariate time series, dynamic thresholding, and attention mechanisms for root-cause anomaly detection in streaming data.

📂 Full Python Code (attention_convlstm_anomaly_detection.py)

# attention_convlstm_anomaly_detection.py

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import tensorflow as tf
from tensorflow import keras
from tensorflow.keras import layers
from sklearn.preprocessing import MinMaxScaler
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
import datetime

# Load multivariate dataset (from Kaggle UCI or other source via pandas)
df: pd.DataFrame = pd.read_csv(
    "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/drscarlat/.../multivariate_anomaly.csv"
)
data: np.ndarray = df.values  # shape (timesteps, features)

# Normalization
scaler: MinMaxScaler = MinMaxScaler()
data_norm: np.ndarray = scaler.fit_transform(data)

# Create sliding windows
def make_windows(x: np.ndarray, window: int) -> np.ndarray:
    N, F = x.shape
    out = np.lib.stride_tricks.sliding_window_view(x, (window, F))[:, 0, :, :]
    return out

WIN: int = 30
windows: np.ndarray = make_windows(data_norm, WIN)

# Build feature images as inner correlations per window
def build_feature_images(wins: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    B, W, F = wins.shape
    imgs = np.zeros((B, F, F))
    for i in range(B):
        imgs[i] = np.corrcoef(wins[i].T)
    return imgs[..., np.newaxis]

X: np.ndarray = build_feature_images(windows)
X_train, X_test = train_test_split(X, test_size=0.2, random_state=42)

# Attention + ConvLSTM Autoencoder
inp = keras.Input(shape=X_train.shape[1:])
x: tf.Tensor = layers.TimeDistributed(
    layers.Conv2D(8, (3,3), activation="relu", padding="same")
)(layers.RepeatVector(WIN)(inp))
x = layers.TimeDistributed(layers.MaxPooling2D((2,2), padding="same"))(x)
x = layers.ConvLSTM2D(16, (3,3), activation="relu", padding="same", return_sequences=True)(x)
q = layers.ConvLSTM2D(16, (3,3), activation="relu", padding="same", return_sequences=True)(x)
att = layers.TimeDistributed(layers.Attention())([q, x])
x = layers.ConvLSTM2D(8, (3,3), activation="relu", padding="same", return_sequences=True)(att)
x = layers.TimeDistributed(layers.UpSampling2D((2,2)))(x)
decoded = layers.TimeDistributed(layers.Conv2D(1, (3,3), activation="sigmoid", padding="same"))(x)

model = keras.Model(inp, decoded)
model.compile(optimizer="adam", loss="mse")
model.fit(X_train, X_train, epochs=30, batch_size=16, validation_split=0.1)

# Compute dynamic threshold
recon_train = model.predict(X_train)
train_loss: np.ndarray = np.mean((recon_train - X_train)**2, axis=(1,2,3,4))
THRESHOLD: float = np.mean(train_loss) + 3*np.std(train_loss)

# Test inference
recon_test = model.predict(X_test)
test_loss: np.ndarray = np.mean((recon_test - X_test)**2, axis=(1,2,3,4))
anomaly_flags: np.ndarray = test_loss > THRESHOLD

# Root-cause: which feature dims have highest contribution
def root_cause(w: np.ndarray, r: np.ndarray) -> int:
    diffs = np.abs(w - r)
    scores = np.mean(diffs, axis=(0,1))
    return int(np.argmax(scores))

root_causes = [root_cause(X_test[i], recon_test[i]) for i in range(len(X_test))]

print(f"Threshold: {THRESHOLD:.4f}")
print("Sample anomalies and root-cause feature index:")
for i, flag in enumerate(anomaly_flags[:5]):
    if flag:
        print(i, "root cause:", root_causes[i])
